english.title: Registered firearms dealer fail to notify sale of firearm within 48 hours
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having, as a registered firearms dealer, sold a firearm, namely **(..SPECIFY FIREARM..), to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) who showed that

(A)_[he]_
(B)_[she]_

was entitled by virtue of section 18(1) of the Firearms (Amendment) Act 1988 to purchase it without holding a firearms certificate, failed to comply with section 18(2) of the Firearms (Amendment) Act 1988 in that you did not, within 48 hours from the transaction, send by registered post or the recorded delivery service a notice of the transaction to the chief officer of police for **(..SPECIFY FORCE..) in whose register the premises where the sale took place were then entered
english.legislation: Contrary to section 18(5) of the Firearms (Amendment) Act 1988.

english.notes:
(i) If the weapon concerned is a shotgun then use H4345.
(ii) Subsections (3) and (4) of section 18 list the matters to be contained in a notice.
(iii) Where the omitted matter is one to which section 18(1A)(a) applies, then (by section 18(6)) the maximum term of imprisonment is three months.
(iv) See also offence wordings H4426 and H4427 re failure to make proper notification of sale.
english.standardstatementoffacts:

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.
(See note (iii) above).

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
